title: `kit-field-sigil_wall`: Sigil wall, field
notes:
- **Mode:** Kit sprite, 256 x 256 transparent sprite, NEW.
- **Save as:** `art/sprites/kit/field/sigil_wall.png`.
- **Shows:** Survival fight maps, old battlefield; the wall of packed mana a Sigil raises: it blocks movement and sight and crumbles away after a while. A hatched square today.
paint: Setting: field, old battlefield (cracked mud, ash, scorched steel plate, sandbag canvas, burnt wood, smoky orange #F68A38, faint ivory mana specks). One Sigil wall sprite, a block of packed mana (nanobots) filling about three quarters of the one-tile cell, square to the grid, straight overhead. It is built of ash-grey flecks with smoky orange sparks, dense and nearly solid in the middle so it reads as full cover that blocks a standing person, with two crossing diagonal strokes of denser flecks laid across its top face as the raised Sigil, an abstract mark and never a letter. The edges are crisp on the top and left and fray into a few drifting motes on the right and bottom, so it looks newly made and about to crumble. A faint inner glow of its own flecks only, no bloom outside it. At 64 px: a bright speckled slab with one bold mark. It must not read as masonry, glass, ice or a stone wall of the setting. Avoid: a brick pattern, a door, a person, a shield, any lettering.
label: Sigil wall, field
prompt:
Paint one game-map kit piece in Heavenprint: hand-painted gouache and ink with broken, directional brush strokes, selective dry-brush scumbling, restrained hatching and warm ivory accents, the same hand as the attached kit pieces, but simplified and bold so it reads at 64 px. Straight overhead view, no perspective tilt, no horizon. Flat, even top light with one consistent soft highlight from the upper left on edges and tops; NO cast shadow, NO drop shadow, NO ground contact shadow, NO glow or bloom spilling outside the object (a lamp, a seam or the flecks the piece names may be lit within the object's own shape, never as a halo). Scale: one tile = 1.5 m = 256 px; a crate is about a metre (about 170 px), a standing person's footprint about a third of a tile. No text, no letters, no numbers, no signs with writing, no logos, no figures, no creatures, no UI, no frame, no border, no watermark. Everything is invented. For a sprite: transparent background (PNG with alpha), the object centred inside an 80% safe box of a 256 x 256 px canvas, crisp clean edges, no halo, nothing touching the canvas edge. For a ground texture: a seamless tileable square texture, 1024 x 1024 px, straight top-down, the left and right edges match and the top and bottom edges match when repeated, flat even lighting, no vignette, no border, no landmark that would show as a repeat, no objects on it, even mid-dark value with gentle low-contrast variation. The piece:

The edges are crisp on the top and left and fray into a few drifting motes on the right and bottom, so it looks newly made and about to crumble. One shallow square raised slab, viewed completely overhead with only the TOP FACE. No camera tilt, no foundation or landscape. Clear 15% transparent margin. Tiny flecks within the slab footprint; the silhouette still reads as one solid blocking object.
